title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:by-construction; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; lever:rl-reward; lever:architecture; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:math; domain:logic; scale:small; model:gemma-2-2b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:falcon3-3b; model:qwen3-4b; metric:internal-external-gap; metric:f-strong; eval:confound-control
tldr: Introduces Structural CoT, where models emit executable computational graphs that compute the answer: far shorter reasoning, but accuracy drops on MATH and memorized answers can bypass the graph.
problem: Free-form CoT is hard to verify, verbose and possibly post-hoc → the answer may not come from the stated reasoning.
method: Model emits an executable JSON computational graph; answer = its deterministic execution. Graph SFT → Graph-Based GRPO (style, graded correctness, node-overlap or proof-F1 rewards; faithfulness runs also emit an answer, with answer and answer–graph consistency rewards). 4 models ≤4B, 5 math/proof datasets.
findings: Beats Graph SFT on all 5 datasets; up to 6.1× shorter than Default GRPO. Internal–external gap ≈0 on iGSM/MATH; F_strong rises (MATH 21.4→40.2), mainly via F_ID. GSM8k+: F_strong 0 and gap widens to 31.9; Qwen3-4B emits memorized original-GSM8k answers, bypassing the graph.
limits: Accuracy cost on MATH (0.19 vs 0.61 Default GRPO). F_OOD (answer follows an edited graph) not consistently improved. Consistency reward directly trains what the gap/F_ID measure. Graph-expressible tasks, ≤4B models only. No code release mentioned.

title: Detecting Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought via Circuit-Guided Internal-External Discrepancy
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:internal-strategy; signal:judge; contribution:metric; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:math; domain:professional; scale:small; eval:ood; model:llama-3.1-8b; metric:internal-external-fgw-discrepancy; metric:detection-accuracy; metric:detection-f1
tldr: Introduces CIE-Scorer, which flags unfaithful CoT from discrepancies between sentence-level circuits and hidden states: beats all baselines on every dataset, but needs white-box access and human labels.
problem: CoT-unfaithfulness detectors rely on text or answer-consistency signals and ignore internal computation; full circuit tracing is too costly for long CoTs.
method: CIE-Scorer: entropy plus counterfactual token selection → sentence-level transcoder circuits → GNN embeddings; FGW distance to a hidden-state sentence graph, margin-trained on FaithCoT-Bench human labels; Llama-3.1-8B.
findings: Best Acc/F1 on all 4 datasets vs 11 baselines (Table 1: Acc +3.3 to +11.5 points); 48-55% less memory than CRV, which runs out of memory on 2 datasets; post-hoc CoTs show feature-level and spurious chains structure-level discrepancy. Code released.
limits: Needs white-box access; one 8B model; supervised, trained per dataset on human labels; weak transfer involving AQuA; F1 gains small (1.4-4.2 points); text claims +5.4 Acc on AQuA vs 3.3 in Table 1; ICLR submission, under review.
relations: compares-to [[lanham2023measuring]]: Adding-mistakes, early-answering and paraphrasing tests run as instance-level detector baselines

title: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:implanted-behavior; lever:sft; lever:preference; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:auditing; domain:chat; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:adversarial; eval:specificity; model:llama-3.3-70b; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-0.6b; metric:behavior-verbalization-rate; metric:auditing-agent-success-rate; metric:sandbagging-claim-rate
tldr: Trains introspection adapters, a shared LoRA that learns via SFT and DPO to report behaviors implanted by finetuning: tops AuditBench on unseen finetunes but often hallucinates behaviors.
problem: Finetuning implants hidden or harmful behaviors; untrained self-reports are unreliable, so auditing is hard.
method: Finetunes of one base with known implanted behaviors (8 categories) → one shared LoRA introspection adapter: SFT to verbalize each behavior, then DPO preferring accurate reports over hallucinations → applied to unseen finetunes.
findings: AuditBench SOTA (59% agent success vs 53% next-best); flags 7/9 cipher-attack models; surfaces 16/52 RM-sycophant behaviors, not root goal; sandbagging claims 33% on UKAISI sandbaggers vs 15.8% FPR. Gains with scale (Qwen3 0.6B→14B: 37.7→77.3%), diversity, DPO. Code, models released.

title: Can Language Models Explain Their Own Classification Behavior?
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-report; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:benchmark; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:synthetic; scale:closed; eval:ood; model:gpt-3-175b; model:gpt-3-13b; model:gpt-4; metric:articulation-accuracy
tldr: Introduces ArticulateRules to test whether LLMs can state the rule driving their own classifications: articulation improves with scale in context, but finetuned models mostly fail, even after SFT.
problem: Can LLMs state the rule that actually drives their own classification behavior?
method: ArticulateRules: 29 procedurally generated few-shot text-classification rules + adversarial OOD inputs; verify behavior matches known rule ID+OOD, then grade MC/freeform rule articulations (GPT-4 grader, ~95% vs human labels). In-context: GPT-3 family, GPT-4; finetuned GPT-3 → SFT on articulations, held-out rules.
findings: In-context freeform acc rises w/ scale: Curie 1%, GPT-3 7%, GPT-4 72%. Finetuned GPT-3 (>90% ID+OOD on 10 rules) articulates 0%; SFT on correct explanations → still 0% on 7/10. MC above chance 9/10 after SFT. Paraphrase/CoT augmentation no sig. help (1 rule tested). Dataset, code, OpenAI eval released.
limits: Success necessary not sufficient (pattern completion vs introspection); black-box only; SFT on 10 rules, low diversity; 2023 OpenAI models only.

title: A False Average: Pooled CoT-Monitor Accuracy Conceals a Reasoning-Dependent Fragility
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; signal:env-label; signal:cot-intervention; signal:judge; lever:inference-time; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:attack; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; contribution:meta-evaluation; motivation:monitoring; domain:agentic; domain:code; scale:closed; scale:large; scale:small; eval:adversarial; eval:behavior-control; eval:held-out-evaluator; eval:measure-validation; eval:monitor-scope; eval:confound-control; eval:ood; factor:action-visibility; factor:cot-controllability; model:gemini-3.1-pro; model:gpt-5.4; model:gpt-5.4-nano; model:claude-sonnet-4.6; model:claude-opus; model:qwen3-8b; metric:tpr-at-fixed-fpr; metric:monitor-auc; metric:probe-auc; metric:suspicion-score
tldr: Shows pooled CoT-monitor accuracy hides fragility: rewriting only the reasoning collapses detection of reward hacks whose intent appears solely in the CoT, while action-visible hacks remain caught.
problem: Pooled CoT-monitor accuracy on reward hacks hides fragility on the ~23% where only the reasoning reveals intent.
method: Terminal Wrench trajectories; one-shot, gradient-free rewrite of the reasoning only (actions byte-identical); scored by a held-out monitor from another family; paraphrase control; trace-only and reference-solution defenses; 810 live-agent rollouts; probes on surrogate monitors.
findings: Subset catch 96%→4-11%; pooled catch drops only ~25 pts; paraphrase 91→85%. Trace-only defenses ≤20%; reference solution 48%. Live hacks nearly all caught, being action-visible (AUC ≥0.996 with innocent narration, 0.97 without). Probe out-reads verdict (AUC 0.94-0.98 vs 0.57-0.69), but a behavioral control shows this need not mean concealed knowledge.
limits: One benchmark and rubric family, LLM-judge monitors; no adaptive attacker; live realized FPR 8-26%, residual too small to give a rate; probe on an open surrogate only. Code released.

title: Necessary but Not Sufficient: Auditing Same-Answer Counterfactuals for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; object:self-prediction; reveals:planted-cue; signal:planted-cf; contribution:metric; contribution:meta-evaluation; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:open-qa; domain:mcq; domain:synthetic; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:behavior-control; eval:confound-control; eval:measure-validation; eval:monitor-scope; eval:scaling; factor:cue-design; model:mistral-7b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-32b; model:qwq-32b; metric:probe-auc; metric:monitor-auc
tldr: Audits same-answer counterfactual tests where probes beat CoT monitors on hint use: a baseline without hidden states does better, and probes fall to chance on prior-matched candidates.
problem: Results where probes beat CoT monitors may track answer identity or candidate priors, not hidden hint provenance.
method: Same-answer label: keep traces giving the hinted wrong answer; dependent if a matched-control hint changes it. Prompt-end probes vs Sonnet-4 judges (incl. CoT+self-report); prior/text baselines, control-state probes, patching. 3 models (7-9B), 4 QA sets.
findings: Probes AUROC 0.61-0.65 vs judges 0.51-0.62 (Llama tie); no-hidden-state baseline 0.76-0.84, adding states gives no lift. Control-state probes match; W−G probes and patching null; prior-matched candidates drop probes to chance. Under prompt injection (N=45-78), judges win. On a synthetic role-swap, state differences win.
limits: Artificial soft hint. Larger-model slices only 35-54 rows. Independent class scarce. Positive result synthetic only. Code not released.
relations: builds-on [[boppana2026reasoning]]: Adopts its probe-vs-CoT-monitor comparison; reads its early answer decoding as non-provenance signal

title: Believe it or Not: Mechanistic Interpretability of Learned Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:planted-cf; signal:implanted-behavior; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; motivation:auditing; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:adversarial; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:measure-validation; eval:confound-control; eval:scaling; model:gemma-3-1b; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:clt-fvu-differential
tldr: Trains a model with GRPO to use hints while hiding them and inspects it with transcoders: concealment-like features appear early but cannot be told apart from format changes.
problem: Unknown what internal computation a model builds when RL teaches it to use MCQ hints while hiding them from its CoT.
method: Model organism: Gemma 3 1B, SFT then GRPO (LoRA) with a -3.0 penalty for mentioning the hint. Gemma Scope 2 CLTs pretrained on the base model act as anomaly detectors: per-layer FVU differential and new-feature counts over with-hint, no-hint and non-MCQ prompts, correct vs wrong hints, and 6 checkpoints.
findings: 98% accuracy with hints vs 38% without, 0% leakage. Added computation peaks at layers 20-23. Two features (L15/f478, L12/f317) new in all 10 tested prompts. Correct- vs wrong-hint differentials correlate at r=0.971, read as content-agnostic concealment. Differential present from step 50 and roughly flat over training: no phase transition.
limits: Hint-specific signal ~10x smaller than total GRPO change, so CLTs cannot separate hiding from format changes. Single 1B model, MCQ only, 20 prompts per condition. Features not functionally characterized. No code release mentioned.
relations: builds-on [[baker2025monitoring]]: organism mirrors obfuscation from penalizing CoT mentions of exploited behavior | builds-on [[chen2025reasoning]]: reuses the hint-in-MCQ-prompt verbalization setup

title: Balancing Faithfulness and Performance in Reasoning via Multi-Listener Soft Execution
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:planted-cf; signal:cot-intervention; lever:rl-reward; lever:sft; updates:explanation; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:optimization-pressure; model:qwen3-14b; model:phi-4-reasoning-plus; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:early-answering-aoc; metric:adding-mistakes-aoc
tldr: Introduces REMuL, which rewards CoTs that multiple listener models can continue to the same answer, plus answer-only SFT: modest gains in both faithfulness and accuracy on out-of-domain reasoning.
problem: CoT sometimes unfaithful to the model's computation; optimizing for faithfulness often costs accuracy.
method: REMuL: GRPO rewards the speaker when 3 diverse 14B listeners, continuing its CoT truncated at 25/50/75%, reach its answer; a separate answer-only masked LoRA SFT restores accuracy. Train on BBH; test OOD on BBEH, ZebraLogic, MuSR, FOLIO.
findings: Hint usage +2.5 avg; acc +1.8 (Qwen3) / +1.5 (Phi4). Early-answering & adding-mistake AOC up on avg (Qwen3); beats MAT-Steer. Faithfulness-only RL most faithful but cuts acc; joint reward makes objectives conflict; hint-optimized RL fails to transfer to AOC. CoTs more legible, shorter, less backtracking. Ablation: multiple diverse listeners needed. Code released.
limits: 14B models, MC reasoning tasks only; AOC, legibility, ablations, sycophancy on Qwen3 only; no error bars. Hint detection by keyword, only on changed answers. Gains small. Slightly more sycophantic (38.6 to 41.8%). In-domain (FOLIO) training raises acc but not faithfulness.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: uses early-answering and adding-mistakes AOC as faithfulness metrics | builds-on [[chen2025reasoning]]: uses sycophantic hint-injection protocol to measure hint usage | builds-on [[emmons2025pragmatic]]: uses its legibility autorater prompt to score CoT legibility

title: Large language models can learn and generalize steganographic chain-of-thought under process supervision
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:hidden-info; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:env-label; signal:judge; lever:rl-reward; updates:explanation; contribution:negative-result; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; domain:synthetic; domain:open-qa; scale:small; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:ood; model:qwen2.5-3b; model:genprm-7b; metric:encoded-cot-rate; metric:penalized-string-frequency; metric:prefill-ablation-accuracy
tldr: Shows that RL penalties on task-critical CoT strings make models switch to substitute encodings that stay load-bearing, preserve accuracy, and generalize to never-penalized strings, on toy tasks.
problem: CoT penalties can hide reasoning but keep behavior. Is the hidden CoT still load-bearing (steganographic)? Does the encoding generalize?
method: PPO, task reward minus regex CoT penalty on task-critical strings: arithmetic, coin flip (Qwen2.5-3B); ExploreToM with held-out names (GenPRM-7B). Prefill, error-injection, name-swap ablations test load-bearing.
findings: Models substitute strings (U+2217 for *, R/L for Heads/Tails), keep >90% arithmetic acc. Fixed R/L prefill drops coin-flip acc 98% → ~55%. ToM encodings (nicknames, initials) transfer to never-penalized names; task score roughly stable. Code released.
limits: Regex monitor only. 3B/7B, toy tasks. 1/3 coin-flip seeds converge. Arithmetic ablation n=5. ToM encodings hand-labeled.
relations: extends [[baker2025monitoring]]: CoT-pressure obfuscation shown to be load-bearing steganography that generalizes to unpenalized strings

title: Breaking the Chain: A Causal Analysis of LLM Faithfulness to Intermediate Structures
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:output-agreement; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:architecture; lever:preference; updates:behavior; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:code; scale:small; scale:mid; scale:large; eval:confound-control; eval:scaling; factor:cot-necessity; model:qwen3-8b; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-32b; model:qwen3-235b-a22b; model:llama-3.1-70b; model:gemma-2-2b; metric:f-id; metric:f-ood; metric:f-strong
tldr: Tests whether LLM decisions follow their own intermediate structures (rubrics, queries, traces) by editing them: often they do not, and offloading execution to tools largely closes the gap.
problem: Schema-guided reasoning produces editable rubrics, checklists, queries or execution traces. Do the final decisions causally follow these structures?
method: Correct or counterfactually edit the model's own mediator on tasks where a deterministic map fixes the new answer, then re-prompt. Metrics F_ID vs F_Strong. 12 open models (1.7B–235B, thinking off) on RiceChem, AVeriTeC, TabFact and CRUXEval. Case studies: tool externalization, stronger prompts, DPO on faithful-vs-stubborn pairs. Code released.
findings: Mean F_ID–F_Strong gap ~18–23 pp on 3 of 4 datasets. Counterfactual edits are followed more often than corrections. CRUXEval: larger Qwen models bypass the trace (inverse scaling). Tools mostly cut the gap below 0.03. Prompting gives inconsistent gains. DPO raises F_Strong (Qwen3-8B RiceChem 0.52→0.73), accuracy flat or up, but Qwen3-8B AVeriTeC stays flat (0.31→0.29).
limits: Needs gold mediators and deterministic mappings. Open models only, non-reasoning mode. DPO tested on two 8B models only, trains directly on the edited-mediator following that F_Strong scores, and the train/test split is not reported.

title: Language Models Fail to Introspect About Their Knowledge of Language
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:self-prediction; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:generic-cf; contribution:analysis; contribution:metric; motivation:explainability; motivation:cognitive-science; domain:classification; domain:text-continuation; scale:small; scale:mid; scale:large; eval:privileged-access; eval:confound-control; eval:measure-validation; eval:scaling; model:olmo-2-7b; model:olmo-2-13b; model:qwen2.5-72b; model:llama-3.1-70b; model:llama-3.1-405b; model:mistral-large-123b-2411; metric:prediction-behavior-correlation; metric:similarity-controlled-self-advantage; metric:meta-direct-kappa
tldr: Tests whether LLMs' prompted grammaticality and next-word judgments reflect their own string probabilities: alignment is weak, with no advantage for the model itself over similar models.
problem: Do LLMs' metalinguistic answers (grammaticality, next-word choice) reflect their own string probabilities, with no fine-tuning?
method: 21 open models, 1.5-405B. Data: BLiMP/Linguistic Inquiry minimal pairs and 4 word-prediction sets (incl. nonsense, random). Correlate model A's prompted preference with model B's log-prob preference. Regress on similarity (seed, base/instruct, family, Direct-Direct r) to test for a same-model effect.
findings: Both methods accurate but kappa about 0.25; in Exp. 1, Meta-Direct r never above .25, even within model. Similarity predicts alignment (Exp. 1 r=.32), but no self advantage, even against OLMo seed variants or among models of 70B and up. Larger models' prompted answers track probabilities better.
limits: Open weights only, >70B 4-bit quantized; two linguistic domains; forced-choice logit readout; null result may not hold for larger closed models. Code and data released.

title: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:correctness; signal:simulatability; signal:cot-intervention; contribution:theory; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; scale:small; eval:confound-control; model:gemma-3-1b; model:llama-3.2-1b; model:qwen2.5-1.5b; metric:trace-legibility; metric:self-legibility; factor:outcome-rl
tldr: Proves RLVR permits unbounded language drift while SFT bounds it: RLVR CoTs grow less legible on novel tasks but barely drift when RL only sharpens existing behavior.
problem: Language drift (odd, illegible CoT language) may erode CoT monitorability, and its causes are poorly understood.
method: Proofs treat drift as KL divergence from human language, for RLVR vs SFT. DAPO vs SFT on GSM8K: three 1-1.5B base models, 5 seeds, iso-accuracy checkpoints. Instruct readers, or sibling seeds, guess the model's answer from partial CoTs.
findings: RLVR permits unbounded drift, SFT bounds it; capping drift caps expected reward. Novel-task Llama/Gemma: RLVR CoTs less legible than SFT (AUC -0.24/-0.17) and drift differs per seed. Qwen, which mostly sharpens existing behavior: virtually no drift vs SFT. Code released.
limits: Only 1-1.5B models, GSM8K only. Reader legibility is only a proxy for drift. Drift-reward theorem untested empirically. Drift is milder than in frontier CoTs.
relations: builds-on [[roytburg2026measuring]]: adapts its design of weaker models reading CoT prefixes to measure legibility | builds-on [[korbak2025chain]]: formally proves its informal claim that outcome RL need not preserve legibility

title: Investigating the Interplay between Contextual and Parametric Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness under Optimization
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:decision-factors; signal:cot-intervention; signal:interp-tool; signal:param-intervention; lever:sft; lever:preference; lever:model-merging; updates:explanation; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; scale:small; eval:optimization-pressure; model:gemma-3-4b; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:llama-3.1-8b; metric:cot-corruption-sensitivity; metric:cc-shap; metric:ff-hard; metric:faithfulness-gain-transfer
tldr: Introduces FaithMATE, training on one CoT faithfulness metric to test transfer: gains flow consistently from parametric to contextual metrics, less reliably in reverse, and inconsistently among contextual ones.
problem: Contextual (CoT/input perturbation) and parametric (unlearning) CoT-faithfulness metrics compared only descriptively; does optimizing one transfer to the others?
method: FaithMATE: best/worst of 40 sampled CoTs under one metric → SFT or DPO (LoRA); measure gain transfer δ on 6 metrics (4 Lanham corruptions, CC-SHAP, FUR). Gemma3-4B/Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B; OpenBookQA, LogiQA. Plus task-arithmetic merging.
findings: Paradigms positively coupled but asymmetric: parametric→contextual consistent (24/30, 23/25); contextual→parametric 40/48, magnitude variable. Contextual metrics don't reliably inter-transfer; Adding Mistake lowers Paraphrasing in 8/12. DPO > SFT. Acc up in all OBQA configs (avg +6–8%), mixed on LogiQA (17/30 up). EA+FT merging amplifies gains; merging hurts Paraphrasing.
limits: ≤8B, MCQ only; offline training only (no RL); metrics treated as unvalidated proxies; parametric metric ~20 min/instance; no code release stated; LogiQA 23/25 excludes Llama SFT (poor contextual results).
relations: builds-on [[tutek2025measuring]]: FUR step-unlearning as parametric metric and training target; adds continuous ff_cont | builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: early answering, adding mistake, paraphrasing, filler tokens as contextual metrics/targets | builds-on [[parcalabescu2023measuring]]: CC-SHAP used as evaluation-only attribution-based contextual metric

title: ReFIne: A Framework for Trustworthy Large Reasoning Models with Reliability, Faithfulness, and Interpretability
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:stated-plan; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:planted-cf; signal:judge; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; lever:rl-reward; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reliability; domain:math; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:ood; eval:human-study; model:qwen3-1.7b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-8b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-llama-8b; metric:disclosure-faithfulness; metric:commitment-faithfulness
tldr: Introduces ReFIne, which trains models with SFT and GRPO to write structured traces with confidence self-assessment: better interpretability, hint disclosure and calibration at similar accuracy, mainly on math.
problem: LRM CoT tuned for acc/efficiency, not trust: traces hard to follow, silently use cues, overconfident.
method: SFT on tagged traces (understanding→facts→plan→think→answer→self-assessment) → GRPO rewarding correctness, format, cross-section refs, calibrated confidence. Vs matched Plain (correctness-only GRPO).
findings: Qwen3-1.7/4/8B: interpretability +44.0%, faithfulness +18.8% (professor-hint disclosure up), reliability +42.4%; commitment faithfulness 0.90–1.00 (QwQ), 0.83–0.94 (MTurk); acc ≈ Plain, 1.16× shorter. Transfers to DS-R1-Llama-8B. Code released.

title: LIFT: Likelihood-Based Intervention Faithfulness Training
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:math; domain:open-qa; scale:small; eval:held-out-evaluator; model:mistral-7b-v0.3; model:qwen3-8b; model:qwen3-4b-2507; metric:step-intervention-logprob-drop; metric:static-intervention-logprob-drop; metric:truncation-logprob-drop
tldr: Introduces LIFT, which swaps CoT steps for irrelevant facts and trains on continuations weighted by the answer-likelihood drop: big gains on likelihood-based faithfulness proxies, usually small accuracy cost.
problem: CoT answers often don't causally depend on the stated steps; prior fixes need human labels/filtering or symbolic solvers.
method: Swap each step for a domain-matched irrelevant fact (Wikidata/arithmetic corpus, style-rewritten), regenerate, score answer log-prob drop → score-weighted LoRA SFT on post-intervention continuations + gold-answer term (η) + KL to base.
findings: Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B/4B: faithfulness x1.4-2 (GSM8K/SVAMP), x4-18 (StrategyQA) vs accuracy-only SFT; untrained static & truncation metrics also rise. Claims no significant acc cost (yet Mistral GSM8K 0.41 vs 0.50). No answer supervision → more faithful, big acc drop. Code/data in supplement.
limits: Proxy log-prob metrics, main one = training signal; ≤8B; in-distribution tests; ~10-24h data gen/model; hand-tuned hyperparams; fact-corpus dependent.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: uses its truncation (early-answering) metric as independent faithfulness check

title: Entailer: Answering Questions with Faithful and Truthful Chains of Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:decision-factors; signal:by-construction; signal:judge; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; lever:inference-time; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:benchmark; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:mid; eval:human-study; eval:ood; model:t5-11b; metric:human-judged-conclusion-follows; metric:human-judged-premise-correctness
tldr: Introduces Entailer, which answers via backward-chained proofs whose premises and steps it self-verifies: no accuracy cost versus direct QA, and humans find most conclusions follow and premises true.
problem: CoT/explanations may be unfaithful (answer doesn't follow) and untruthful (model doesn't believe its own premises).
method: T5-11B fine-tuned on EntailmentBank + new crowd-labeled entailments (incl. negatives); backward-chains from each answer hypothesis, overgenerates premises, keeps steps the model self-verifies (premises + entailment); answer = top-scoring proof.
findings: Zero-shot OBQA/QuaRTz acc 75.2/75.4 vs direct 75.2/74.1 → no acc cost. Humans (1-deep proofs, 100 OBQA Qs): >70% conclusions clearly follow (Macaw 34%), ~90% premises correct, preferred 57% vs 23%. Mixing with direct QA breaks faithfulness on 14-17% of questions. Data + models released.
limits: Faithful only by answer selection; belief = "yes" to "Is X true?". Near-tautologies, invalid steps; ~360 s/question; one model, science MCQ.

title: Unlearning Deceptive Behaviors in LLMs with Contrastive Forget Sets
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:output; object:cot; reveals:latent-belief; reveals:planted-cue; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; motivation:reliability; motivation:monitoring; domain:open-qa; domain:agentic; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:confound-control; eval:measure-validation; eval:later-rl; model:qwq-32b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b; metric:judged-deception-rate; metric:cue-acknowledgment-rate; metric:tug-of-war-score
tldr: Introduces Pact, unlearning pressure-induced deception via honest traces acknowledging the pressure: deception nearly vanishes and, unlike distillation, CoT still mentions the pressure, though brief deceptive training restores it.
problem: Deception is context-conditional; unlearning targets facts. Suppression (NPO) leaves deception; BCT-style neutral-target distillation removes it but blinds models to the context (benign instructions, secrets, CoT mentions of the pressure).
method: Forget set of own answer flips between pressure and neutral contexts, belief held (sycophancy, MASK). Pact: LoRA SFT on the honest trace prefixed by an acknowledgment of the pressure, plus a benign system-prompt retain set. Compared with NPO, DPO and distillation.
findings: QwQ/R1-32B deception 50–67% → 1.0–2.5%. Traces mention the user 99/98% vs 34/14% under distillation. Secrets and adherence kept; ToW 0.94/0.86. GSM8K/MMLU within 4 pts. Ten deceptive steps undo removal; attack-aware hardening (on distillation) holds them but cuts trace mentions to 7/4%. Code released.
limits: Two 32B models. Eval mostly instructed sycophancy. Keyword trace metric. LLM judge, no human agreement. LoRA only, one seed per row. Hardening not combined with Pact. Monitor value of the restored mentions untested.
relations: compares-to [[chua2024biasaugmented]]: counterfactual distillation (BCT recipe, neutral context) baseline; removes deception but context-blind | builds-on [[chua2024biasaugmented]]: Pact edits BCT-style own-unbiased-response targets to acknowledge the pressure

title: On the Hardness of Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; lever:steering; updates:behavior; contribution:negative-result; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:logic; scale:small; scale:closed; model:llama-3-8b; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:gpt-4; metric:early-answering-aoc
tldr: Tests whether in-context learning, fine-tuning or activation editing can make CoT more faithful: gains are small and inconsistent, often cost accuracy, and activation editing gives no significant gain.
problem: Can standard steering tools (ICL, fine-tuning, activation editing) make the CoT faithful, i.e. make the answer depend on it?
method: ICL and LoRA SFT on self-generated (Q, CoT, A) triplets picked uniformly or by faithfulness (deterministic/stochastic, correct-only variants); ITI-style editing of probe-selected heads. Faithfulness = per-instance early-answering AOC. AQuA, LogiQA, TruthfulQA.
findings: ICL/SFT: small gains that depend on dataset and model, often with an acc drop (~20% vs GTA baseline, Llama SFT on TruthfulQA). Text says faithful demos beat uniform ones; appendix tables mixed. Steering: no significant gain; best heads/alpha/K differ by dataset. GPT-4 is the most accurate and the least faithful.
limits: One truncation metric. 3 datasets. GPT-4 gets ICL only (FT blocked by API errors); steering on Llama-3-8B only. Many differences not significant (p-values in appendix). No code mentioned.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: adopts early-answering metric, made per-instance with answer probabilities

title: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:output; reveals:misbehavior; signal:env-label; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:theory; contribution:benchmark; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:code; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:ood; model:llama-3-8b; model:gemma-3-12b; model:gemma-3-27b; model:llama-3-70b; metric:honest-policy-rate; metric:original-model-probe-score; metric:representation-change; metric:probe-auc
tldr: Maps outcomes of RL against a deception probe on a hackable task: honesty, blatant deception, or probe evasion via text or activations, honesty requiring high KL and penalty.
problem: Training against white-box deception probes may teach evasion, not honesty; prior obfuscation evidence only from artificial harmful-output setups.
method: MBPP-Honeypot RLVR (1 visible test + length penalty → hardcoding); GRPO + off-domain deception-probe penalty; KL × penalty sweep; probe score split: original-model vs representation change.
findings: Outcomes: honest, blatant, obfuscated policy (evasive text, e.g. justifications; low KL + weak penalty), obfuscated activations (RL drift, even w/o probe; PG adds no activation pressure, probe gradients do). High KL + high penalty → honest, no capability cost. Code/models released.
limits: High KL often impractical at scale; obfuscated policies hard to detect; single-turn MBPP, ≤70B; richer hacks (test tampering) untested.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:decision-factors; signal:planted-cf; signal:generic-cf; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:social-bias; scale:closed; model:text-davinci-003; model:claude-1.0; metric:biased-context-accuracy-drop; metric:unfaithfulness-explained-by-bias
tldr: Shows that unmentioned biasing features, such as few-shot answers always being A or a suggested answer, sway CoT predictions, with explanations rationalizing the biased answer instead.
problem: Plausible CoT may misstate the real reasons for predictions → unwarranted trust, and CoT-based audits can be fooled.
method: Biasing features the CoT never mentions (Answer-is-Always-A, Suggested Answer) on 13 BBH tasks; BBQ with swapped weak evidence. GPT-3.5 & Claude 1.0, ZS/FS, CoT vs No-CoT.
findings: Bias verbalized in 1/426 explanations. Accuracy drops up to 36% (ZS); FS CoT less unfaithful. 73% of sampled unfaithful CoTs argue for the biased answer; 15% have no obvious errors. BBQ: up to 62.5% of unfaithful pairs stereotype-aligned (50% = unbiased). Debiasing prompt helps Claude. Code released.
limits: Necessary but not sufficient test. Only small input edits. Two closed models. No fix proposed.

title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tags: source:trustme; source:faith-improvement; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:later-rl; eval:ood; eval:specificity; model:llama-3.1-8b; metric:effective-cue-influence-rate; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:balanced-accuracy
tldr: Introduces VFT, SFT on CoTs edited to acknowledge prompt cues before RL: models learn cue-based reward hacks but verbalize them, leaving far fewer undetected hacks than RL alone.
problem: RL-learned reward hacks (exploiting prompt cues) go unverbalized in CoT → CoT monitors miss them.
method: VFT: SFT on CoTs minimally edited (Claude 4 Sonnet) to credit planted cues (2 cues) → GRPO rewarding cue-aligned wrong MMLU answers incl. held-out cues; vs BCT, RL-only.
findings: Post-RL undetected hacks (ECR) 6% vs 88% RL-only, 99% BCT; verbalization 8%→43% (VFT)→94% (RL). Holds, smaller gap, on non-amplified cues (ECR 15% vs 63-66%). Pre-RL specificity 96-97%. MMLU acc 73→70% after VFT; post-RL ≈ RL-only (63 vs 65%).
limits: Llama-3.1-8B, MMLU only; held-out cues similar to training; post-RL verbalizations vaguer, some over-verbalization; ambiguous cases judged as verbalized; hacks need no CoT.
relations: builds-on [[turpin2023language]]: uses its cued-vs-uncued counterfactual test to find unfaithful CoTs and score faithfulness | builds-on [[chen2025reasoning]]: adopts its flawed-reward RL environment where cues mark rewarded wrong answers | compares-to [[chua2024biasaugmented]]: BCT baseline; reduces cue use pre-RL but relearns cues, verbalization drops to 1% | builds-on [[chua2025deepseek]]: borrows prompt cues from its cue set

title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; signal:param-intervention; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:human-study; model:llama-3-8b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:mistral-7b; model:phi-3-mini; metric:ff-hard; metric:ff-soft
tldr: Introduces FUR, which unlearns CoT steps from the weights to test whether answers depend on them: answers often flip, and this parametric faithfulness barely tracks human plausibility judgments.
problem: Context perturbation tests measure self-consistency, not parametric faithfulness: models can recover erased steps from weights.
method: FUR (PFF instance): unlearn each CoT step's content words (NPO+KL, FF2) → no-CoT answer flips (ff-hard) or loses probability (ff-soft)? Controls: efficacy, specificity, MMLU. 4 LMs, 5 MCQA sets.
findings: MMLU ~unchanged; answers often flip, mostly more than Add-mistake; efficacy tracks ff-hard (r=0.889). Post-unlearning CoTs argue for other answers (GPT-4o-mini judge). ff-soft vs human plausibility r=0.15. Code released.
limits: Only CoT/no-CoT-agreeing instances; lower bound, no recall guarantee. Imperfect unlearning; needs weights; costly per step. English MCQA, ≤8B.
relations: compares-to [[lanham2023measuring]]: Add-mistake and paraphrase baselines; FUR flags more CoTs as faithful | contradicts [[lanham2023measuring]]: context perturbations may underestimate faithfulness; truncation/filler-insensitive (post-hoc) CoT can still be faithful | compares-to [[parcalabescu2023measuring]]: CC-SHAP baseline attempted, NaN on 90.24% of instances; adopts self-consistency distinction

title: Markovian Transformers for Informative Language Modeling
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:hidden-info; reveals:correctness; signal:cot-intervention; signal:by-construction; lever:architecture; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:text-continuation; scale:small; eval:held-out-evaluator; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:mistral-7b; model:qwen3-4b; model:phi-3.5-mini; metric:perturbation-fragility; metric:cross-model-informativeness
tldr: Trains Markovian language models with RL to answer from a length-capped CoT alone: CoTs become more perturbation-sensitive and help other models answer, with accuracy slightly below unconstrained RL.
problem: Standard CoT is not load-bearing: the answer can bypass the reasoning, so the CoT may not reflect the decision.
method: Markovian bottleneck: answer predicted from length-capped CoT alone, question hidden. GRPO-style RL on ln P(ans|CoT) vs a frozen-baseline CoT, actor-reward grads, KL to base; LoRA.
findings: GSM8K 19.6→57.1%, ARC 36.1→79.9%; mean ≈3–4 pp below Non-Markovian GRPO (MMLU 13 pp). Larger drops under CoT perturbation than Non-Markovian (Wiki, most QA; not arithmetic). Llama CoTs help Mistral/Phi/GPT-2 predict GSM8K answers. Code released.
limits: Ensures sufficiency, not mirroring of internals; post-hoc CoT still possible. Steganography only argued against (KL, transfer). ≤8B; no human study; ~$20K compute.

title: Reasoning Models Will Sometimes Lie About Their Reasoning
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:stated-plan; signal:planted-cf; signal:output-agreement; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:explanation; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; eval:measure-validation; eval:scaling; factor:cot-length; factor:cot-necessity; model:qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking; model:kimi-k2.5; model:claude-haiku-4.5; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:hint-intent-honesty; metric:hint-use-honesty
tldr: Tests whether reasoning models asked to flag unusual input admit hint use: they reliably notice hints but mostly deny intending to use them, while their answers follow them.
problem: Hint-based faithfulness evals never tell models how to treat unusual input. Open question: when explicitly asked, do LRMs report relying on hints?
method: Chen et al. hints (re-created templates; 4 types, correct/incorrect) on GPQA-Diamond and 200 MMLU-Pro items. Prompt asks the model to flag unusual content and state its intended use; hint use is permitted. A GPT-5.4 judge labels presence, intent and use. Metrics: normalized F̄, H̄_I, H̄_U.
findings: Hint-presence F̄ is high (perfect for metadata and unethical-info hints). Yet models mostly deny intending to use hints while their answers follow them; Qwen H̄_I is near zero. H̄_U higher for Qwen and Kimi; Claude often never mentions the hint again. Weak intent-use alignment. No consistent difficulty trend; budget shifts Claude's scores, not Qwen's. Code released.
limits: Three LRMs, MCQ only, single sample at temperature 0. Judge checked by one author on 50 Claude CoTs (κ 0.69–0.87). No own no-instruction baseline: the comparison is to Chen's numbers on other models. Lenient honesty definition.
relations: extends [[chen2025reasoning]]: adds unusual-content instructions and intent/use honesty scores to its hint eval

title: PINTO: Faithful Language Reasoning Using Prompt-Generated Rationales
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:simulatability; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; model:t5-base; model:roberta-large; model:gpt-neox-20b; metric:leakage-adjusted-simulatability; metric:perturbed-rationale-acc-drop
tldr: Introduces PINTO, training a small reasoner with counterfactual regularization to use rationales from a prompted LLM: better accuracy, especially out of distribution, and greater reliance on rationales.
problem: Rationale-augmented reasoners can ignore or misuse rationales (shortcuts) → rationales unfaithful; self-rationalization needs >100B LMs or costly rationale annotation.
method: Frozen GPT-NeoX-20B prompted (7 demos) → choice-specific rationales; T5-base reasoner fine-tuned w/ counterfactual regularization: label-smoothed (low-confidence) targets when rationale masked or 30% tokens replaced.
findings: Best ID acc in most cases, best OOD among rationale methods; T5: higher LAS except OBQA (CSQA 24.22 vs 18.75 std); larger acc drop under swapped rationales; biggest gain from human rationales. Acc rises, no cost. Code released.
limits: Faithfulness = reasoner's reliance on another model's rationale; StrategyQA LAS low for all (PINTO 3.35); RoBERTa reasoner: LAS not best on CSQA/QASC; <1B reasoners, commonsense MCQ only.

title: SCOTT: Self-Consistent Chain-of-Thought Distillation
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:generic-cf; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:human-study; model:t5-3b; model:gpt-neox-20b; metric:leakage-adjusted-simulatability; metric:rationale-perturbation-sensitivity; metric:rationale-refinement-gain
tldr: Introduces SCOTT, which distills CoT from a teacher using contrastive decoding and trains the student with a counterfactual loss: rationales become more consistent with answers at comparable accuracy.
problem: Distilled CoT rationales are vacuous (teacher hallucinates) and ignored (student answers via question→answer shortcuts) → rationale-answer inconsistency.
method: GPT-NeoX-20B teacher rationalizes gold answers via contrastive decoding (vs empty/wrong answer) → T5-3b student SFT with factual + counterfactual loss (wrong-answer rationale → wrong answer).
findings: CD-wrong teacher most consistent. CD students generally higher LAS than CoT prompting, greedy/human-rationale students; counterfactual loss adds more. Comparable acc (human-rationale student slightly higher). More perturbation-sensitive, bigger refinement gains. Larger students more accurate, less faithful; gains hold across sizes. Code released.
limits: Extra teacher forward pass + counterfactual data. LAS needs T5-large simulator. Knowledge-intensive QA only; perturbation/refinement on CSQA, CREAK only.

title: Causally-Enhanced Reinforcement Policy Optimization
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:open-qa; domain:code; domain:professional; scale:small; eval:ood; model:llama-3-8b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:phi-3.5-mini; model:qwen3-4b-thinking-2507; model:qwen3-1.7b; metric:jacobian-coherence-score
tldr: Introduces CE-PO, an RL reward adding Jacobian-based influence scores linking prompt, rationale and answer: beats vanilla RL on accuracy, but faithfulness is checked only with its own scores.
problem: Outcome-only RL → correct answers paired with spurious/unfaithful CoT; shortcut learning, reward hacking.
method: CE-PO: Jacobian influence scores for Z→X, X→Y, direct Z→Y (prompt→rationale→answer), hardened by projecting out token-shuffled counterfactual subspace; power-mean fused with BERTScore → PPO/GRPO reward.
findings: +5.49 pts avg acc over vanilla (up to 9.58); both CE variants beat BERTScore-PPO/GRPO on avg for all 5 models, 4 test sets; OOD gains (Qwen3-4B only). Unhardened or partial Jacobian reward → length hacking. Scores higher on judge-correct samples. Code released.
limits: ≤8B only. Faithfulness gauged only by own Jacobian scores; no independent CoT test; abstract's unfaithful-CoT and perturbation-robustness claims not directly tested. First-order proxy, not true DCE. Acc via GPT-4o-mini judge; ablations and OOD on one model each.

title: Enhancing the Outcome Reward-based RL Training of MLLMs with Self-Consistency Sampling
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:reasoning-validity; signal:cot-intervention; signal:judge; lever:rl-reward; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:multimodal; domain:mcq; domain:math; scale:small; eval:ood; model:qwen2.5-vl-7b; model:qwen2.5-vl-3b; model:internvl3-8b; metric:flawed-reasoning-correct-answer-rate; metric:distinct-answers-after-truncation
tldr: Introduces SCS, an RL consistency reward from resampling truncated multimodal reasoning under image noise: raises accuracy across RL algorithms and modestly reduces correct answers reached through flawed reasoning.
problem: Outcome-reward RL on multimodal MCQ rewards lucky guesses after a faulty CoT like genuine reasoning → unfaithful traces reinforced.
method: SCS: truncate rollout, resample continuations under Gaussian image noise; answer agreement → consistency reward, added to accuracy + format rewards in RLOO, GRPO, REINFORCE++ variants.
findings: Qwen2.5-VL-7B avg acc (6 benchmarks): +7.7 pp RLOO, +0.9–2.0 pp others; +3.2 / +1.6 pp on 3B / InternVL3-8B (RLOO). Vs. base model, correct answers with flawed reasoning ~15% rarer (human 25.0→21.2 per 100; o3-mini, Gemini agree). Code released.
limits: Multimodal MCQ only, ≤8B. Faithfulness = step correctness, checked by authors vs. reference solutions (+ LLM raters), 100 correct cases/benchmark; no vanilla-RL comparison. RLOO baseline below SFT. ~+38% train time despite "negligible" claim.

title: Evaluating honesty and lie detection techniques on a diverse suite of dishonest models
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:output; object:self-report; reveals:latent-belief; reveals:hidden-behavior; reveals:own-uncertainty; signal:planted-cf; signal:implanted-behavior; signal:judge; lever:sft; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:steering; updates:explanation; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:auditing; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:chat; scale:closed; eval:ood; eval:specificity; eval:adversarial; eval:confound-control; eval:measure-validation; eval:monitor-scope; eval:scaling; model:claude-3.7-sonnet; model:claude-3.5-haiku; metric:honesty-rate; metric:monitor-auc
tldr: Benchmarks generic honesty and lie-detection methods on dishonest Claude model organisms: honesty fine-tuning with prompting helps most, and prompted self-classification detects lies better than probes.
problem: Without task-specific supervision, can generic techniques make models lie less (state what they believe false) and detect their lies?
method: 5 lying testbeds (Harm Pressure, Password Lock, Secret Side Constraint, Auditing MO, MASK) on Claude 3.7 Sonnet/3.5 Haiku; compare prompting, generic honesty SFT, honest-persona SFT, steering/fuzzing; lie detection via prompted self-classification, truth probes.
findings: Honesty SFT lifts honesty 27%→52%, 65% stacked with honesty prompting; self-classification baseline AUROC 0.82, best 0.88; probes, steering, persona SFT underperform.
limits: Blog, not peer reviewed; stylized organisms, no coherent deception; Claude only; judge-based labels; little technique tuning. Honesty and Harm Pressure data released.

title: Self-Critique and Refinement for Faithful Natural Language Explanations
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:inference-time; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; eval:behavior-control; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:mistral-7b-v0.3; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:falcon3-7b; metric:counterfactual-unfaithfulness-rate
tldr: Introduces SR-NLE, a training-free loop refining post-hoc explanations with self-feedback: important-word feedback beats free-text critique and cuts counterfactual unfaithfulness, though random words do similarly on e-SNLI.
problem: Post-hoc NLEs leave out the input words that actually drive the prediction.
method: Training-free self-refine loop (SR-NLE): answer → NLE → feedback (free-text critique, or top-5 important words via prompting/attention/IG) → refine, up to 3 rounds. Scored with the Atanasova CF word-insertion test. 4 7–8B models on ComVE, ECQA and e-SNLI.
findings: Avg unfaithfulness 54.81% → 36.02% (IWF-Attn). IWF beats NLF in every setting; NLF beats self-consistency sampling only on avg. Prompted IWF ≈ attribution IWF. Largest gain in round 1. Answers fixed, so no acc change. Code released.
limits: Single string-match CF metric. Refined NLEs get longer. Random-word feedback ≈ IWF (e-SNLI). Post-hoc NLEs only, <10B models. IG is costly.

title: CASE: Causal Alignment and Structural Enforcement for Improving Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; lever:architecture; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:theory; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; scale:small; eval:ood; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-8b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-7b; metric:filler-tokens; metric:early-answering-aoc; metric:indirect-effect; metric:direct-effect
tldr: Introduces CASE, which blocks the instruction-to-answer shortcut with counterfactual SFT data and an inference-time attention mask: best combined faithfulness in every setting, including cross-dataset transfer, at similar accuracy.
problem: Answer can bypass the CoT via a direct instruction→answer (Z→Y) shortcut.
method: Standard CoT SFT plus answer-only loss on counterfactual-CoT, biased-instruction and empty-instruction data; inference-time mask blocks answer→instruction attention. Mutual-information bound analysis. Three 7–8B models; ARC, StrategyQA, LogiQA.
findings: Best G-mean of FT/EA/CIE/CDE in all 12 settings: +37% avg vs per-setting strongest baseline (incl. untuned base), +61% in cross-dataset transfer. Avg acc 74.88 vs 74.80%. SFT mainly lifts CIE/CDE; mask lifts FT/EA. Code released.
limits: ≤8B; MCQ/boolean QA only. CIE counterfactuals use the same generator and prompt as the training data. Mask leaves instruction info in CoT states. T/F tasks need partial masking (β=80%); CDE worse than base on StrategyQA for 2 of 3 models.

title: From Concept Alignment to Causal Grounding: An Intervention Test of Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:internal-strategy; reveals:decision-factors; signal:interp-tool; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:math; scale:small; eval:measure-validation; eval:confound-control; eval:scaling; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:gemma-2-2b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:qwen3-1.7b; model:qwen3-8b; metric:shared-concept-ablation-drop; metric:cc-sae; metric:sae-concept-jaccard; metric:prediction-grounded-recall
tldr: Tests with SAEs whether CoT reuses the concepts behind a direct answer and whether ablating them matters: concept overlap is high but barely predicts the ablation effect.
problem: Behavioral and attribution tests of CoT faithfulness ignore internal computation. Does the CoT reuse the concepts behind the direct answer, and do those concepts causally drive it?
method: One off-the-shelf SAE per layer encodes the answer-position residuals of a no-CoT pass and a CoT-conditioned pass. Three overlap metrics (CC-SAE, Jaccard, recall), plus Δp, the drop in answer probability when the shared features are ablated. 5 open models from 1.7B to 9B; GSM8K, LogiQA, OpenbookQA, ARC-Easy.
findings: Overlap is high but barely predicts Δp (lift 1.08). Random and norm-matched ablations give far smaller Δp. Δp mostly peaks at mid-to-late layers. Qwen3 is distributed across layers, Llama-3.1-8B localized. Larger models in a family score higher. Causally important shared concepts are not always verbalized in the CoT.
limits: Only models of 9B or less; only items where CoT and no-CoT answers agree. Relies on pretrained SAEs (Δp robust to width/sparsity, r>0.8); no ground truth. Comparison with prior metrics only on Llama-3.1-8B/LogiQA (ρ 0.10–0.30). Verbalization claim rests on hand-picked case studies. No code release stated; under review.
relations: extends [[parcalabescu2023measuring]]: Moves CC-SHAP-style self-consistency from input attributions to the SAE concept space (CC-SAE) | compares-to [[lanham2023measuring]]: Early answering, filler, mistakes, paraphrase correlate only weakly with Δp (ρ≈0.10) | builds-on [[zaman2025causal]]: Uses its continuous prediction-score versions of the Lanham metrics | compares-to [[tutek2025measuring]]: FUR correlated with Δp (ρ=0.25); also adopts its two-pass agree-only setup | compares-to [[shen2026detecting]]: CIE scores, supplied by the authors, correlated with Δp (ρ=0.30) | builds-on [[sun2026investigating]]: Follows its parametric (FUR) faithfulness setup for the metric comparison

title: Doing What They Say, Not What They Reason: Locating the Faithfulness Gap in LLM Agents
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:reasoning-validity; reveals:stated-plan; signal:output-agreement; signal:env-label; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:meta-evaluation; contribution:benchmark; contribution:metric; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:social-simulation; domain:agentic; domain:game; scale:closed; scale:large; eval:measure-validation; factor:model-preference; model:claude-haiku-4.5; model:gemini-2.5-flash-lite; model:deepseek-reasoner; metric:conclusion-action-inconsistency; metric:rule-misapplication-rate
tldr: Locates the faithfulness gap in LLM poker agents: actions almost always match stated conclusions, but conclusions sometimes misapply the agents' own stated rules, which a mechanical-rule prompt halves.
problem: Do LLM agents act on the reasoning they state? Social simulations have no reference behavior to check this process fidelity against.
method: Texas Hold'em multi-agent simulator with a Monte Carlo reference action. The gap is split in two: conclusion→action (DECISION tag vs JSON action, compared with a free-text parser) and reasoning→conclusion (DECISION vs the agent's own stated EQUITY/POT_ODDS/RULE; stated equity vs Monte Carlo flags input errors). Four prompt strategies, plus a "mechanical rule" prompt ablation.
findings: Explicit-tag conclusion→action inconsistency is 0.7–1.8% across the three models; the free-text parser's 22–26% (Haiku, Flash-Lite) is a parsing artifact. Rule misapplication is a third of Haiku's interpretable errors but 8% of DeepSeek's, and 99.5% of Haiku's misapplications are risk-averse. The mechanical prompt halves misapplication (13.9→6.8%) and raises adherence 8 points. Injecting the rule does not reliably raise adherence. Code released.
limits: Three API models; diagnostic run on only two, mechanical ablation on Haiku only. Poker is not a social simulation. The reference is a threshold heuristic, not true GTO. Verbose elicitation may change behavior. DeepSeek parse rate is 62%. χ² tests treat decisions as independent.

title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; reveals:internal-strategy; signal:planted-cf; signal:by-construction; signal:env-label; contribution:benchmark; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:open-qa; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:code; domain:agentic; domain:synthetic; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; eval:adversarial; eval:monitor-scope; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-235b-a22b; model:gpt-oss-120b; model:gpt-5; model:gemini-3-flash; model:claude-sonnet-4.5; metric:monitorability-score
tldr: Introduces MonitorBench, an open benchmark testing whether CoT reveals decision-critical factors: monitorability is low when factors only set the answer, falls with capability, and drops under concealment prompts.
problem: No comprehensive, fully open benchmark of when CoT reveals decision-critical factors; prior evals small, fragmented, partly closed.
method: 1,514 instances / 19 tasks: cue & goal injection, dual objectives, impossible tasks, necessary steps. Qwen3-32B monitor, 3 scopes (CoT/action/all). Monitorability = flag rate, TE-normalized for injections. 8 LLMs. 2 prompt stress tests (direct concealment, monitor-aware evasion).
findings: High when factor shapes reasoning, low when it only sets the answer (Cue-Answer, deception). More capable → less monitorable (r −0.87 to −0.39). CoT-only beats action-only by ~24%. Stress tests cut Cue-Answer ~27%, via omission not obfuscation. Code released.
limits: Objective tasks only; black-box. Closed models expose only summarized CoT. Single LLM monitor, weak human agreement on agent traces. Prompt-only stress tests; 5 instances per agent task.
relations: extends [[guan2025monitoring]]: scales its intervention/process/outcome monitorability framework to 19 open tasks plus stress tests

title: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:planted-cf; signal:judge; contribution:metric; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:open-qa; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:professional; scale:small; eval:ood; model:qwen3-4b; model:llama-3.1-8b; metric:balanced-accuracy; metric:probe-auc
tldr: Introduces VERITAS, which maps layer-wise residual states to faithful and unfaithful token anchors to detect unfaithful CoT: beats judge and probe baselines and transfers across subsets and models.
problem: LLM judges and static activation probes flag unfaithful CoTs but cannot show how unfaithfulness develops across layers and generation.
method: VERITAS: J-lens maps layer-by-phase residual states to token anchors mined from within-question faithful/unfaithful pairs; Map, Profile and Dynamics features feed a logistic regression; tested on BonaFide and FaithCoT-Bench.
findings: Mean balanced accuracy 0.749 (Qwen3) and 0.737 (Llama3.1), against best baselines of 0.655 and 0.644. Anchors transfer across subsets (97-99% retained); cross-model transfer retains 81-89%.
limits: Two small replay models read CoTs mostly written by other models. Needs labelled pairs. Configuration chosen by best balanced accuracy. HLE-Bio stays near 0.6. LLM-judge baseline only 7-8B; the abstract's +28.4% gain over it does not match Table 1. Code only promised.
relations: builds-on [[gurarieh2026faithfulness]]: uses BonaFide diversionary-hint CoTs and their faithfulness labels for training and evaluation | compares-to [[lanham2023measuring]]: early-answering baseline; VERITAS outperforms it on all datasets | compares-to [[li2025better]]: Info Gain logit-based baseline; VERITAS outperforms it

title: Attention is not not Explanation
tags: source:background-2026-10-21; object:external-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:interp-tool; contribution:metric; contribution:meta-evaluation; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:professional; scale:small; eval:measure-validation; model:bilstm; model:mlp; metric:diagnostic-mlp-f1; metric:tvd-jsd-tradeoff
tldr: Argues that attention can be an explanation, against Jain and Wallace: learned attention guides a simple model better than adversarial attention, and per-instance adversaries overstate manipulability.
problem: Jain & Wallace's case against attention as explanation rests on per-instance adversarial attention detached from the model that computes it, with no baseline for normal variance; whether attention explains depends on the definition (plausible vs faithful).
method: Reproduce J&W's BiLSTM + additive attention on 6 binary tasks (SST, IMDb, AG News, 20News, MIMIC Diabetes/Anemia). Four tests: uniform-attention baseline; variance across 8 random seeds; diagnostic non-contextual MLP whose token outputs are weighted by frozen guide attention; model-consistent adversary trained with loss TVD(to base predictions) − λ·KL(from base attention), swept over λ.
findings: Uniform attention matches learned on AG News, 20News (dropped), SST borderline. Base-LSTM attention is the best MLP guide (Diabetes F1 0.753 vs 0.699 learned, 0.404 uniform). Trained adversaries reach mean JSD >0.4 at base-level F1 but are poor guides (Diabetes 0.503, SST 0.592, IMDb 0.700; Anemia 0.932 the outlier). Convex TVD/JSD curves support manipulability, but J&W's per-instance setup exaggerates it; seed variance already large for Diabetes negatives. Attention is "an" explanation, not "the" one; exclusivity not needed for plausibility. Code released.
limits: LSTM binary text classification only (no QA, NLI, seq2seq); English; no human evaluation, functionally grounded proxies only. Best adversary per dataset picked on test-set F1; SST epochs selected on test loss.
relations: builds-on [[jain2019attention]]: reproduces its BiLSTM + additive attention setup, datasets, splits and TVD/JSD measures | contradicts [[jain2019attention]]: per-instance adversarial attention exaggerates manipulability; model-consistent adversaries are less extreme and fail as MLP guides, so attention is not disproved as explanation

title: Measuring Association Between Labels and Free-Text Rationales
tags: source:background-2026-10-21; object:posthoc-expl; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; signal:interp-tool; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; eval:measure-validation; model:t5-base; metric:robustness-equivalence; metric:feature-importance-agreement
tldr: Proposes robustness and feature-importance tests of whether self-rationalizing models link labels to free-text rationales: the tested joint models pass both, with labels and rationales degrading together.
problem: Faithfulness work focuses on extractive rationales; for free-text rationales from joint (self-rationalizing) models there was no way to test whether predicted label and rationale are linked, so rationales may be made up.
method: Five T5-Base variants per dataset on e-SNLI and CoS-E v1.0/v1.11: pipeline I→R;R→O (faithful by construction) vs joint I→OR ("label explanation: rationale"). Rationale quality = accuracy of IR→O minus I→O on gold labels. Two label-rationale association tests on I→OR: robustness equivalence (Gaussian noise on input embeddings; label flips vs rationale quality); feature importance agreement (gradient attributions w.r.t. label vs rationale logits, validated with ROAR; occluding top-k% tokens by one should hurt the other output more than random).
findings: Pipelines suit reasoning tasks poorly: I→OR rationales give R→O higher accuracy than I→R ones (CoS-E v1.0 62.0 vs 53.5) and score higher quality; gold free-text rationales are not sufficient (IR→O beats R→O by 12.2 pts CoS-E v1.11, 1.1 e-SNLI). I→OR passes both tests on all 3 datasets: labels and rationales stay stable together at low noise and degrade together (CoS-E v1.0: σ² 0–15 vs 20+); label-attributed occlusion degrades rationales beyond random and vice versa. Code released.
limits: Tests are necessary, not sufficient, conditions for faithfulness. T5-Base only, 2 English tasks. Quality metric uses gold labels, can be negative and confounds rationale with label quality; 82.5% agreement with one author's judgments (60 instances). Joint training costs accuracy on CoS-E (−4.3/−6.1 pts vs I→O).
relations: builds-on [[jacovi2020towards]]: answers its call for graded faithfulness evaluations; aims to place free-text rationalizers on its faithfulness spectrum | builds-on [[hase2020leakageadjusted]]: rationale-quality score is a gold-label variant of automated simulatability, justified by its human-correlation results

title: Bootstrapped Monitoring: Leveraging Transparent Reasoning to Oversee Stronger AI Agents
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; signal:env-label; lever:prompt-pipeline; contribution:method; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:agentic; domain:code; scale:small; scale:large; scale:closed; eval:adversarial; eval:monitor-scope; eval:confound-control; eval:specificity; factor:cot-length; model:glm-5; model:kimi-k2.5; model:deepseek-v4-pro; model:gpt-5.4; model:qwen3-8b; model:gpt-4.1-mini; metric:tpr-at-fixed-fpr
tldr: Proposes bootstrapped monitoring, where a weak trusted model audits an untrusted monitor's transparent CoT for collusion: usually beats trusted-only monitoring given raw CoT, but not summarized CoT.
problem: As the capability gap widens and frontier CoT turns opaque, weak trusted monitors may no longer reliably judge agents' actions.
method: An untrusted monitor with transparent CoT scores the agent's actions, and a weak trusted model audits that CoT and verdict for collusion. Tested on BashArena side tasks with prompted collusion (default, needle, codewords) and automated red teaming, scored as catch rate at ≤3% FPR.
findings: With raw CoT, beats trusted-only under collusion in most cells (worst prompt loses on short GPT-5.4 rollouts with GPT-4.1 Mini T). Catch rises from ~60% to ~95% with rollout length (~30% per-step leak). Red teaming cannot push detection below 80% on long rollouts, but reaches ~20% on short ones until blue-team re-prompting of T restores ~70% catch. With summarized CoT (GPT-5.4), below trusted-only in 5/6 cells, ~28pp on average.
limits: Collusion is prompted, not trained. BashArena only. Red teaming on two configurations. Preprint, no code release mentioned.

title: Monitorability as a Free Gift: How RLVR Spontaneously Aligns Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; signal:cot-intervention; factor:outcome-rl; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:code; domain:logic; scale:small; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5b; model:qwen3-4b; metric:g-mean-squared; metric:draft-reliance; metric:draft-answer-consistency; eval:ood; eval:specificity; eval:scaling
tldr: Tests whether RLVR improves CoT monitorability as a free side effect: gains come early then plateau, depend on training data, and track entropy drops rather than capability.
problem: Is RLVR's "free gift" of CoT monitorability universal, a capability side effect? What drives it?
method: GRPO (task+format reward) on Math/Code/Science/IF data & mixes, DS-R1-Qwen-1.5B & Qwen3-4B; track hint g-mean² (Qwen2.5-32B monitor), D2A draft-swap, entropy, attention; ablate train length, difficulty.
findings: Gains early, then plateau; data-dependent (Science training can hurt); IF data, diversity, IF cascade best; weak/negative capability link (IF-only cuts DS-1.5B acc); tracks entropy drop & prompt attention, not answer→CoT; longer train length, hard train/eval data → lower.
limits: ≤4B models; mechanisms correlational; input-intervention metric may reward prompt sensitivity ("false sense of monitorability"); D2A agreement weaker on DS-1.5B general tasks; no code release mentioned.
relations: builds-on [[guan2025monitoring]]: adopts g-mean² metric, hint, sycophancy and sandbagging intervention evals | extends [[chen2025reasoning]]: systematizes early-RL faithfulness gain then plateau across domains and models | builds-on [[chua2025deepseek]]: hint-based intervention setup cited as source alongside Chen and Guan

title: Faithful Logical Reasoning via Symbolic Chain-of-Thought
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:correctness; signal:judge; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; motivation:explainability; domain:logic; domain:mcq; scale:closed; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:gpt-4; metric:unfaithful-correct-rate
tldr: Introduces SymbCoT, an LLM-only pipeline that translates logic problems to symbolic form, reasons with rules and verifies each step: beats CoT and solver baselines, with fewer flawed-but-correct answers.
problem: NL CoT imprecise for logic; solver offloading (Logic-LM) brittle to translation errors and info loss, and gives little explanation.
method: Few-shot, LLM-only pipeline: translate to FOL/CO → plan → solve with symbolic rules over hybrid NL+symbolic premises → verifier checks translation & each step, refines.
findings: GPT-4: beats CoT & Logic-LM on all 5 logic sets; 100% execution rate. Human-judged correct-but-flawed answers (FOLIO): CoT 6%, SymbCoT w/o verifier 2%, full SymbCoT 0%. Code released.
limits: Faithfulness = human validity rating, FOLIO only, no causal test; GPT-3.5/4 only; more tokens/API cost; GPT-3.5 FOLIO below Logic-LM.
relations: builds-on [[pan2023logiclm]]: reuses Logic-LM's five datasets, test records, GPT models and baseline numbers | compares-to [[pan2023logiclm]]: main solver baseline; SymbCoT higher accuracy (except GPT-3.5 FOLIO) and execution rate | contradicts [[pan2023logiclm]]: LLM-only symbolic CoT beats solver offloading on GPT-4; Logic-LM held solvers more reliable than LLMs

title: Investigating CoT Monitorability in Large Reasoning Models
tags: source:idea-reports-2026-10-19; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:math; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:measure-validation; eval:specificity; eval:scaling; factor:cot-length; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-7b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-14b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-30b-a3b; metric:effective-cue-influence-rate; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:undetected-misbehavior-rate; metric:false-positive-rate
tldr: Measures how cue verbalization and monitor reliability interact in reasoning models: monitors rarely miss cue use but over-flag, and longer CoTs go with more verbalization and less scheming.
problem: CoT monitoring needs faithful cue verbalization and reliable monitors; how the two interact has not been studied.
method: 8 planted cues; MCQ (AIME converted to MCQ, GPQA, MMLU-moral); 6 open LRMs, 1.5B-30B; Robustness, Scheming, EEMR, OSM; GPT-5-nano verbalization judge, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite monitor; 8 CoT-shortening or -lengthening interventions on Qwen3-4B.
findings: Scheming up to 45% under Unauthorized Access (above 40% for 2 models); monitors rarely miss (avg EEMR at most 3.6%) but over-flag (OSM 54.7% for Qwen3-14B), and OSM rises with accuracy; on Qwen3-4B longer CoT goes with more verbalization (r=0.629) and less scheming (r=-0.630); compression hurts.

title: Introspecting Alignment Shifts Beyond Behaviors Implanted Through Fine-Tuning
authors: Yoshida, Gomezjurado Gonzalez, Yamamoto et al.
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:wild-cf; lever:sft; lever:preference; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:benchmark; motivation:auditing; domain:safety-refusal; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:specificity; model:qwen3-14b; model:gemma-3-12b; metric:shift-classification-accuracy; metric:shift-classification-macro-f1; metric:report-coverage; metric:report-precision
tldr: Tests introspection adapters on Hugging Face fine-tunes with unintended alignment shifts: they generalize to unseen models, the proposed DAIA beats LoRA adapters, though a probe sometimes wins.
problem: Introspection adapters (IAs) have mainly been tested on deliberately implanted behaviors. Real fine-tunes shift alignment as side effects that nobody labeled.
method: 213 HF PEFT fine-tunes of Qwen3-14B/Gemma3-12B; LLM-judge-scored harmful-compliance shift vs base on 13 safety categories → 5-way labels + LLM-written reference reports; SFT (+DPO for free-form) IAs; DAIA adapter processes base output & fine-tuning delta in separate branches.
findings: IAs generalize to unseen models and categories. DAIA's average beats LoRA-IA in all OOD splits (OOD-C 41.3 vs 35.3) and gives better free-form reports. A probe beats both IAs on OOD-B classification (54.1 avg). Patching: DAIA uses the FT delta more. Code + data released.
